claims.text: The initial material is a coarse-grained, metastable alloy with non-optimized properties.
Severe plastic deformation can enhance phase stability in a metastable material.
Severe plastic deformation can refine the microstructure of a metastable material.
Severe plastic deformation can optimize material properties.
High-pressure torsion and equal-channel angular pressing are applicable severe-plastic-deformation methods.
Room-temperature processing under controlled high strain rates can avoid excessive temperature-induced phase transformations.
Severe plastic deformation increases dislocation density.
Severe plastic deformation generates high-angle grain boundaries and an ultrafine-grained structure.
The high density of defects and refined microstructural features induced by severe plastic deformation can thermodynamically stabilize desired phases.
The high density of defects and refined microstructural features induced by severe plastic deformation can kinetically stabilize desired phases.
Defect generation and microstructural refinement from severe plastic deformation can enhance mechanical properties.
Defect generation and microstructural refinement from severe plastic deformation can enhance functional properties.
The severe-plastic-deformation-processed material will have greater phase stability than the unprocessed baseline.
The severe-plastic-deformation-processed material will have finer grains than the unprocessed baseline.
The severe-plastic-deformation-processed material will have improved mechanical or functional properties relative to the unprocessed baseline.
Excessive strain or heat can cause unwanted phase transformations or introduce deleterious defects, limiting the effectiveness of severe plastic deformation.
